summary: The note covers a September 5, 2023 power outage on the Eastern seaboard that is under investigation and attributed to a sophisticated cyberattack. It explains why the power grid is vulnerable, how attacks on operational technology work, and recent incidents. It also describes industry mitigation, government and international roles, public pressure, and future technologies and workforce efforts.
one_line: Overview of the September 2023 Eastern seaboard outage, suspected cyberattack, grid vulnerabilities, and the industry, government, and international responses to protect power grids.
key_facts: On September 5, 2023, a significant power outage hit multiple Eastern seaboard cities; it is still under investigation and points to a sophisticated cyberattack.
On September 21, Southern Power in Georgia reported a minor disruption caused by a ransomware incident that entered through an unsecured remote access point.
On October 3, 2023, the Grid Security Corporation thwarted an attempted breach by quickly isolating the affected systems, preventing widespread outages.

Cyberattacks of greatest concern in the power sector target operational technology (OT), the hardware and software managing electricity flow, where intrusions can have immediate physical consequences.
Cyber analyst James O'Connell said attacks can involve malware that lies dormant, evading detection until triggered.
Attackers exploit vulnerabilities such as outdated software and weak passwords to cause outages, physical damage, or data theft.

NERC's Critical Infrastructure Protection standards are mandatory; spokesperson Michael Lee said on September 30, 2023 that noncompliance can bring fines up to a million dollars per violation, per day.
Utility defenses include regular risk assessments, patching systems, phishing training, strong authentication, physical security, and continual network monitoring.
The Department of Homeland Security has increased collaboration with the energy sector, and CISA provides tools and resources to critical infrastructure owners, per Lauren Kim on October 25, 2023.
Daniel Torres of the International Energy Agency said on November 11, 2023 that threat actors often operate from abroad, exploiting international legal loopholes.
Anita Vasquez, a local energy provider spokesperson, said on November 4, 2023 that customer trust is paramount and motivates cybersecurity investment.
Future measures include AI and machine learning, decentralized grid architectures, advanced encryption, blockchain, and industry-academia programs training workers in both energy and cybersecurity.
